name: Aidan Dewar
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nourish (virtual dietitian / nutrition-care platform, New York)
profile: Aidan Dewar co-founded Nourish in 2021 with childhood friend Sam Perkins and Stephanie Liu, and runs it as CEO. Nourish matches patients with insurance-covered registered dietitians via telehealth; it raised a $70M Series B led by J.P. Morgan Growth Equity in 2025 (reported >$1B valuation) and a $100M Series C led by Menlo Ventures in May 2026 at a reported $1.75B valuation.
interesting_fact: Nourish was reported to be profitable at the time of its 2025 Series B, unusual for a fast-growing digital-health startup; its 2026 Series C was framed around supporting patients on GLP-1 treatments.
deep_cut_fact: Dewar and his co-founder Sam Perkins are childhood friends; the third co-founder, CTO Stephanie Liu, was Perkins' friend from Princeton.
notes: Founder story is personal (he has spoken about his own chronic condition motivating Nourish) - let him raise it. Unverified aggregator claims: Harvard economics (2018), prior consulting, co-founded 'Feed The Frontlines SF' - not confirmed. Has appeared on podcasts (e.g. PodRocket episode on going $0 to $1B).

name: Alice Bentinck
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Entrepreneurs First (EF), talent investor / company builder (lives in San Francisco)
profile: British entrepreneur (b. 1986) who left McKinsey to co-found Entrepreneurs First with Matt Clifford in 2011, a programme that backs exceptional individuals before they have a co-founder or idea. She became CEO in December 2023; in March 2026 EF raised $200M at a $1.3B valuation and is pivoting to act as a bridge between Europe and the US. She also co-founded Code First Girls.
interesting_fact: Code First Girls, which she co-founded in 2012 after noticing most EF applicants were male, has taught over 250,000 women to code for free; she received an MBE in 2016 and co-wrote the award-winning book 'How to be a Founder' (Bloomsbury, 2022) with Clifford.
deep_cut_fact: Her first business was at school: at Godolphin School in Salisbury she joined Young Enterprise and created a business model for handmade purses. Before McKinsey she also interned in Tony Blair's office, assisting the Africa Governance Initiative.
notes: Very accessible, frequent podcast guest and speaker; EF is highly media-friendly. Relevant angles: EF's 2026 US-centric strategy and $200M raise. No published press email found on joinef.com (web search budget ran out before a deeper check).

name: Steve Sonnenberg
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Awardco (employee recognition and rewards platform, Lindon, Utah)
profile: Steve Sonnenberg founded Awardco around 2011 with his cousin Mike Sonnenberg, building an employee recognition and rewards platform whose key differentiator is an integrated Amazon Business catalogue with no markups. Awardco raised a record HR-SaaS Series A in 2021 and a $165M Series B led by Sixth Street Growth in May 2025 at a valuation above $1B, and says it serves 3,000+ organisations.
interesting_fact: Amazon initially rejected Awardco's plan to show Amazon products on its platform; after Amazon Business launched in 2015 he was invited to pitch at Amazon HQ, and the partnership became Awardco's core advantage.
deep_cut_fact: He started Awardco by borrowing $5,000 to buy the domain name Awardco.com; for the first four years he sold the product himself while his wife helped fulfil orders by hand.
notes: Utah-based; tells his comeback story openly (started Awardco after a prior small company failed in 2011) - but don't lead with it. Awardco hosts the RCGNZ Summit in Park City (Nov 2026). No published press email found.
